headline: Army plans Iowa explosives detonation despite court order
pages: The US Army says it will go ahead with detonating about five tonnes of degraded explosives in Iowa, even though a court ordered a halt. A filing by the Justice Department on Saturday said the Army needs to act now to protect personnel and nearby communities. The Army now plans to act by Nov. 24 under an emergency exemption. The material is lead azide, stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. The Army says falling temperatures raise the risk of an accidental blast, and that removing the bunker doors for the planned detonation left the material more vulnerable. Environmental groups sued, arguing the Army did not weigh safer alternatives, and a court paused the work.
The EPA granted an emergency permit covering 68 drums. Residents were earlier told to leave their homes for six hours. No new date or details have been released. Source: BBC News.
